concept: The family's week is drawn as a signal box's illuminated track diagram: steel-cyan lines painted on green-black slate boards, a lamp at every stop, and times hung in a timetable margin beside the line. A line is drawn only where there is an order: the fortnight runs across Home from a lit now lamp to its last stop, the setup steps run across, To do and the plans hang down a timetable, the newest ideas and Status's chain of who answers drop from the ring at their head, and Vera's conversation hangs from her screen to a lit ring at the message box, where it is your turn. Sets with no order keep their lamps but no rail. The page should feel exact, calm and easy to read: the lamps show how things stand at a glance, slate carries every page, and #6dff9c is lit only for what is happening now or live.
companions: One companion, steel-cyan #a7c4d8, fixed at :root as --steel so no section can reset it. It is the diagram's wiring and the family's hand: links and section-head links (underlined); the ring round every page's icon (the glyph inside keeps its section's colour); 'here' in the bar (a 16% steel cell with a steel hairline, a 3rem lit segment of the rule and a lamp at its centre) and in the phone's tab bar; the current tab's cap; the Settings nav's latched item and lamp; today's cap on the month; the family's chat avatars and the 3px bar on their bubbles; the ring where their messages join the line. Dimmed to #394652 and #58697a it draws every rail and ring edge. Green-black slate is the material: #0f1519 trays behind every list (Home's sections, To do, Status's columns and panels, the Ideas grid, Settings, the month), #161c20 square plates on #262e35 edges, a #0f1519 bar, and a quieter steel #a3b3bf for labels. The section and kind colours keep their learned values and work only in lamps, icons and tints: cyan stops on Coming up, the plans and the month; lemon rings on To do with filled amber when late; pink gift lamps for the kids; each kind's ring as a new idea's lamp and each idea plate tinted 7-9% with its kind (4-5% for the warm kinds). A cobalt wash, #4f66e0 at 2.4, lights the greeting's top right corner opposite the green pool (sampled (25,34,47)).
decisions: Kept every line as a system on every page: the bar's rule with its lamp under the current page; the masthead line that rings the page icon, turns its corner and runs under the title; the fortnight line with its breathing now lamp; the To do timetables on Home and the To do page; Chat's thread from Vera's screen to the box, on the phone too; the tracks on Status, Plans, Settings, setup, Sign in and the 404. The lamp legend holds everywhere: hollow ring to come, lit sage done, amber needs a look, red ring off, #6dff9c only for now and live.

A ring is a terminus. It is drawn only where a line leaves it: every masthead, Lately added (newest first) and Status's 'Who answers' (a primary-to-fallback chain), whose rail now drops from the ring through the head to the first lamp however the head wraps. Every other head icon (Coming up, To do, the kids, Keys, Connected to, What it has cost, the Status panels, the Settings cards) is set bare in its section's colour in the same 1.95rem cell, so all heads still line up over one column.
Lines only where there is order. The kids' two lists and Status's Keys and Connected to keep their lamps and plates but lose the joining rail, so they read as a lamp column on a board, not a route.

Steel-cyan owns 'here', links, rings, tab caps and today on every page. The base sheet resets --accent per section, so the draft's Ideas bar segment and tab cap came out lilac, Home's To do link lemon and the month's today cyan; all of them now use --steel. The 'here' cell went from 8% to 16% steel with a hairline, so it survives the squint beside the segment and lamp.

Fixed a silent fault: the theme writes the page-wide roles as values, not properties, so every var(--heading), var(--label) and var(--bubble) in the draft resolved to nothing. Both chat bubbles were transparent and plate titles inherited. The four roles are now defined at :root, and Vera's bubble is the green-black glass it was meant to be.

Chat on the desktop is read as a timetable: ring, a dotted leader, the time, then the family's words flush right, with the time beside its bubble rather than 470px away in the margin. Only Vera's times and the day stay in the margin by her screen. The family's avatars are steel on slate, never amber. On the phone the two sides separate (the family 3rem in from the left, Vera 2.5rem clear of the right, the steel bar on the left), and a rail runs down the left gutter through Vera's screens to a lit ring above the box.

Every timetable margin is headed once, 'DUE' in the legend's tracked caps, so each stamp is only a value on one line: '2 days ago', 'yesterday', 'in 2 days 19:56' on Home (with the hour in ink beside the day), '27 Sep 19:56' on the To do page. Home's margin went from 8.35rem to 7rem and its plates carry only who, on one line. Below 40rem the legend folds away and each stamp moves into its plate's head, prefixed 'Due'.

The To do page joined the system: its list sits on a slate board with the 'DUE' legend beside '4 shown', the repeated 'Open' tag is hidden (the filter already says Open), the time-zone note is a footnote under the list, the plates are about 10px shorter, and 'Add something to do' is set like Ideas' 'Save a thought for later' (DM Sans 600 1rem), so fold summaries are one control everywhere.

The Plans month carries the legend: each plan is a small slate plate with an 8px lamp, a cyan ring to come, lit sage once past, and today's is the breathing now lamp. Past days' numerals and plans step back to faint. Today's cap is steel. The 'Google Calendar is not connected' note is the masthead's deck, aligned with the title, on the month and the list.

Home: Send is the last thing on the From row, after the mic, on Home as in the chat (on the phone the picker flexes and Home's 'From' is read out but not shown, so Send never wraps), which trimmed the greeting by 54px. Coming up's plates show only the hour in tabular mono, because the day numeral above already names the day. Home is now 1750px, down from 1790px.

Status: the three column boards stretch to share a bottom edge like a panel; 'Who answers' uses Vera's plain speech icon in its ring; the 404's line ends on a red ring (off) at the centre of 'Back to the start', so every line on the site ends on a lamp.

Typesetting: Archivo at 84% gets word-spacing 0.08em, so 'Not found' and 'Sign in to FamilyDB' no longer close up. Stamps are values in sentence case (mono, tabular, 0.75rem, no tracking); mono caps are kept for legends only (eyebrows, weekday heads, 'DUE'). Field labels are one drawing on every page, DM Sans sentence case, the ask's 'From' and the Ideas and To do filters included. The kids' counts are in DM Sans tabular, so '0 open' is never read as 'Ø open'.

Kept from the draft: Archivo 84% for titles (3.05rem), heads (1.42rem) and day numerals; DM Sans for what people and Vera say; DM Mono tabular for stamps; VT323 on the tubes only; the thinner, squarer case with an 8px radius, groove, vents and power LED; kind-tinted idea plates; square tick wells, never lamps; 2.75rem targets (1 of 56 on Home under 44px, the skip link, and 1 on every other page).
strengths: A structure no other entrant has, now held as a rule: a line is drawn only where there is an order, a ring only where a line begins, and a lamp at every stop, the same on Home, To do, Plans, Chat, Status, Settings, Sign in and the 404.

Grounded colour below the fold everywhere: slate boards carry Home's sections, the To do page, Status's columns and panels, the Ideas grid, Settings and the month; the steel companion reaches every page, section pages included.
Chat reads at a glance on both screens: her lines from her screen, the family's flush right in steel, each message's time beside it, the day named once, and the line ending in a lit ring at the box.
Glow is scarce and meaningful: below the fold #6dff9c appears only as the breathing now lamp, live Status lamps, today on the month and the rings where it is your turn.
Clear typesetting: three faces with separate jobs, a real step from title to head to plate to body, one-line tabular stamps under one legend per margin, and one drawing for field labels.
Usability: Send on the From row everywhere, a square tick well apart from the lamps, 'here' marked by cell, segment and lamp, and 2.75rem targets on every page.
weaknesses: Still a line-heavy design. Home carries four lines (setup, Coming up, To do, Lately added) and a judge who reads lines as a subway map may still see one, even though each now has an order.
Its colour is the same slate and steel-cyan as the other slate entrants; the difference from them is in structure and type, not in palette.
The To do page cannot light a late task amber, because that page is not told which tasks are late (Home is); its overdue tasks show hollow lemon rings like the rest.

Home's words differ from today's by 4.4%: 3.3 points are the clock (today's shot was taken within 24 hours of Vera's last line, so it shows her brief reply on Home), and the rest is the timetable legend replacing 'was due' and 'due' on each stamp.
Home's greeting still stacks the ask box and the ways to start above the fold; Home is 1750px, longer than the one-line listing designs.
Numbers in Status's tables keep DM Mono's slashed zero, which the kids' counts no longer use; the tables are the machine's figures, so this is on purpose, but it is a second zero on one site.
revisions: Defined --steel at :root and moved every 'here', link, tab cap, ring, today and nav mark onto it, so section scopes no longer turn them lilac, lemon or cyan; raised the 'here' cell to 16% steel with a steel hairline.

Found and fixed that --heading, --label, --bubble and --bubble-them were never defined as properties (the theme writes them as values), which had left both chat bubbles transparent; they are now defined at :root.

Rails only on ordered lines: dropped the joining segments on the kids' lists, Keys and Connected to; ran the rail up through the head into the ring on Lately added and Who answers; set every other head icon bare in its section colour in the same cell; Settings card icons bare in steel.

Chat: the family's time now sits at the leader's end, beside its bubble; family avatars are steel on slate, not amber; on the phone the sides separate with the steel bar kept on the left, and a rail runs through Vera's screens to a lit ring above the box.

To do page: on a slate board, one 'DUE' legend beside '4 shown', one-line '27 Sep 19:56' stamps, the 'Open' tag hidden, the time-zone note moved under the list as a footnote, the add summary set in DM Sans 600 1rem, and plates about 10px shorter.

Plans month: plans are plates with lamps (ring to come, sage once past, the breathing now lamp today), past days fade, today's cap is steel, and the source note is the masthead's deck (on the list too).
Home: Send last on the From row (desktop and phone), Coming up plates show only the hour, To do's margin 7rem with one 'DUE' legend and one-line stamps with the hour beside the day, who on one line.
Status boards stretch to one bottom edge; Who answers shows Vera's plain icon; the 404's line ends on a red ring centred on its button.

Typesetting: word-spacing 0.08em on the condensed heads; stamps in sentence case with no tracking; field labels in DM Sans everywhere; the kids' counts in DM Sans tabular; 'DUE' and eyebrows keep mono caps as legends.

Declined: making sentence case narrow the Home stamps. In a monospace face lowercase is exactly as wide as caps, so 'was due 2 days ago' still overran 7rem; the width came instead from naming the margin once ('DUE') and stamping only the value.

Bent: on Home's To do the note asked for '19:56 · Alex' as one facts line on the plate; I moved the hour into the margin beside the day instead ('in 2 days 19:56'), so Home and the To do page hang the whole 'when' in the same place and the plate carries only who.

Resolved a contradiction in the notes: the kids' lists were to have their rail both run up into the head ring and dropped as an unordered set. I dropped it (no order, so no line), and with no line leaving the head, its icon is bare.
